title: Scala Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Print a greeting
entries.summary: @main marks a starting function. println prints text.
notes: Keep the indented body under the function.

entries.name: Keep a fixed value
entries.summary: val names a value that cannot be reassigned.
notes: Use var only when reassignment is needed.

entries.name: Build a message
entries.summary: An s string can insert a variable with a dollar sign.
notes: The s before the quotes enables interpolation.

entries.name: Choose a result
entries.summary: An if expression can return one of two values.

example.code:
@main def lesson(): Unit =
  val score = 8
  val message = if score >= 5 then "Pass" else "Try again"
  println(message)

notes: An expression that must return a value needs both branches.

entries.name: Store a list
entries.summary: List holds items in order. head reads the first item.
notes: head fails on an empty list; headOption is safer when it may be empty.

entries.name: Transform every item
entries.summary: map builds a new list by applying a function to each item.

entries.name: Keep matching items
entries.summary: filter keeps items for which its function returns true.
notes: The underscore stands for the current item here.

entries.name: Name a calculation
entries.summary: def defines a function. Its input and return type are shown with colons.
notes: The returned result must match the declared type.

entries.name: Handle an absent value
entries.summary: Option holds Some(value) or None. getOrElse gives a fallback.
notes: Calling get on None throws an error.

entries.name: Match a named choice
entries.summary: match checks cases from top to bottom. _ is a catch-all case.

example.code:
@main def lesson(): Unit =
  val light = "green"
  val message = light match
    case "red" => "Stop"
    case "green" => "Go"
    case _ => "Wait"
  println(message)

notes: Keep case lines indented under match.

entries.name: Group data fields
entries.summary: A case class is a handy data type with named fields and value-based equality.

example.code:
@main def lesson(): Unit =
  case class Book(title: String, pages: Int)
  val book = Book("Moon Trip", 24)
  println(book.pages)

notes: copy creates a new value rather than changing the old one.

entries.name: Combine a list
entries.summary: foldLeft starts with one value and combines it with each list item.
notes: The starting value affects the final result.
